title: Learning inverse folding from millions of predicted structures
layout_note: Three columns: training structures on the left, the model in a framed box in the centre, training sequences on the right. Left: two rows, 'Predicted structures (12 million)' over 'CATH structures (~16,000)', each led by a filled disc whose size stands for the dataset size (a large magenta disc, a small dark-purple one) with a faint grey ribbon render behind the labels; arrows labelled 'Span masking' / 'Noise' run into the model box. Right: 'UniRef50 sequences (12 million)' and 'CATH sequences (~16,000)' over pale grey wavy lines, with arrows labelled 'Supervision' pointing left into the box. A magenta dotted line labelled 'AlphaFold2' runs over the top from the UniRef50 sequences back to the predicted structures.
grouping: One thin black rectangle titled 'Inverse folding model' holds the network; everything about data sits outside it. Colour ties each dataset's structures to its sequences: magenta for the predicted / UniRef50 pair (disc, labels and the AlphaFold2 loop), dark purple for the CATH pair.
shapes_depth: The network is a diagonal stack of thin slabs in perspective, shaded from dark slate (GVP) through purple (Encoder) to light blue (Decoder) with a soft shadow; the stage names are set rotated along the stack in matching colours, '(Generic Transformer)' in grey. A curved arrow labelled 'Invariant features' points into the stack. Datasets are flat discs; structures and sequences are only faint grey textures (ribbon render, wavy lines) behind coloured text.
proposed_highlight: The magenta data path is the paper's point: the large magenta disc dwarfs the CATH disc, and the magenta AlphaFold2 loop shows where the extra structures come from; the model itself is drawn in cool colours inside a plain frame.
lesson: Show a data-scale argument with filled discs sized by dataset size and one colour per dataset carried to its paired sequences, and draw the structure-from-sequence step as a dotted loop over the model from the sequences back to the predicted structures.
notes: Venue = bioRxiv preprint: the PDF header reads 'this version posted April 10, 2022' (v1; venue_source: pdf); no conference version was checked. elements 'other' = the dataset-size discs. The layer slabs and the ribbon render are embedded images recorded by refs crop and left out of the palette.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: inverse folding (structure to sequence) trained on predicted structures
taxonomy.note: paradigm GVP = Geometric Vector Perceptron (GVP-GNN); crop opened from the build cache at kb-build/protein-structure/crops/esmif1/fig1.png because kb fetch-crop had no recipe

insights.structure: Three columns: structure datasets on the left, one thin black frame titled 'Inverse folding model' in the centre, sequence datasets on the right, with a dotted magenta 'AlphaFold2' line arching over the top from the right column back to the left.
insights.data: Each dataset is a filled disc sized by dataset size (large magenta for 12 million predicted structures, small dark purple for ~16,000 CATH) over a faint grey ribbon render; sequences are faint grey wavy lines; the network is a diagonal perspective stack of slabs shaded dark slate (GVP) to purple (Encoder) to light blue (Decoder).
insights.emphasis: The magenta data path (big disc, 'Predicted structures', 'UniRef50 sequences', AlphaFold2 loop) is the only warm colour, so the data-scale argument dominates while the model sits in cool tones inside a plain frame.
insights.flow: Structures enter left-to-right via arrows labelled 'Span masking' / 'Noise'; sequences enter right-to-left via 'Supervision' arrows; the AlphaFold2 loop returns over the top, so the figure reads as a closed cycle rather than a pipeline.
insights.avoid: The discs are not area-proportional (12 million vs ~16,000 is ~750x but the large disc is only ~9x the small one's area), and the grey ribbon and wavy-line textures are so faint they barely read as data.

arrangement.units: one framed box for the model in the centre; datasets unframed outside it on both sides
arrangement.inputs_as: dataset-size discs with coloured names and faint ribbon / wavy-line textures
